summary: Adds a batch read endpoint to LabelEngine that returns labels for a set of object IDs in a single HTTP call.

classification.why_platform: This is a generic read capability over the existing labels.object_labels schema. It carries no domain meaning — it exposes raw label records keyed by caller-supplied UUIDs. Any application consuming LabelEngine can use it.
non_goals: Filtering by label name within the batch

consumes: labels.object_labels table (Postgres, schema owned by LabelEngine Sprint01)
labels.labels table (Postgres, schema owned by LabelEngine Sprint01)
provides: POST /api/objects/labels/batch — given a list of object_ids and an object_type, returns all attached labels for each object_id in one response
Zero-fill guarantee: every requested object_id appears as a key in the response, even if it has no labels attached
invariants: Response keys exactly match the input object_ids list (no extras, no omissions)
Labels within each object's list are ordered by attached_at ASC, label_id ASC (consistent with existing per-object ordering)
object_type is always required; requests without it are rejected 422
Requests with more than 200 object_ids are rejected 422 BATCH_TOO_LARGE before any DB query
An empty object_ids list returns an empty map immediately without a DB query
failure_modes: 422 OBJECT_TYPE_REQUIRED — object_type missing or empty string
422 OBJECT_IDS_REQUIRED — object_ids field missing from body (Pydantic validation)
503 DB_UNAVAILABLE — connection pool exhausted or DB unreachable

provides: BatchLabelRecord — { id: str, name: str, attached_at: str (ISO-8601) }

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/objects/labels/batch
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return labels for multiple objects in one call; zero-fills missing object IDs

exposed_surfaces.name: LabelService.get_labels_for_objects
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Execute a single parameterized SQL query for a batch of object_ids and object_type; return a dict keyed by object_id

internal_flow.name: validate_request
internal_flow.description: Router receives POST body. If object_ids is empty, return {} immediately. If len(object_ids) > 200, return 422 BATCH_TOO_LARGE. If object_type is missing or empty-after-strip, return 422 OBJECT_TYPE_REQUIRED.

internal_flow.name: query_db
internal_flow.description: Call LabelService.get_labels_for_objects(conn, object_ids, object_type). Service executes one query: SELECT ol.object_id, ol.label_id, l.name, ol.attached_at FROM labels.object_labels ol JOIN labels.labels l ON l.id = ol.label_id WHERE ol.object_id = ANY(%s) AND ol.object_type = %s ORDER BY ol.attached_at ASC, ol.label_id ASC.
outputs: list of raw rows: (object_id, label_id, label_name, attached_at)

internal_flow.name: build_response
internal_flow.description: Service initialises result dict with all requested object_ids mapped to empty lists (zero-fill). Iterates DB rows and appends BatchLabelRecord to the appropriate key. Returns BatchLabelsResponse.
outputs: BatchLabelsResponse with all requested object_id keys populated

internal_required.role: new Pydantic models: BatchLabelsRequest, BatchLabelRecord, BatchLabelsResponse
existing router file — new route added here

forbidden: Direct SQL access from router (all DB access via LabelService)
Separate DB queries per object_id (must be a single batched ANY(%s) query)
Any application-specific logic or domain interpretation

platform_implementer: Add BatchLabelRecord, BatchLabelsRequest, BatchLabelsResponse to app/models.py
Add get_labels_for_objects(conn, object_ids, object_type) to LabelService in app/service.py using ANY(%s) query; zero-fill from input list
Add POST /api/objects/labels/batch route to app/routers/objects.py with validation logic from internal_flow step 1
Route must be placed before the per-object routes to avoid FastAPI matching 'labels' as an object_id in /api/objects/{object_id}/labels — verify route ordering in objects.py
test_writer: Happy path: two objects each with labels — verify both appear with correct label lists and ordering
Partial hit: one object has labels, one has none — verify zero-fill (empty list, not absent key)
Empty object_ids: verify immediate {} return, no DB call
object_type mismatch: request object_type does not match stored attachment object_type — verify labels from other types are NOT returned
All requested IDs have no labels: verify all keys present with empty lists
reviewer: Confirm route ordering in objects.py: /api/objects/labels/batch must not be shadowed by /api/objects/{object_id}/labels
Confirm zero-fill is implemented from the input list, not the DB result set
Confirm ALL(%s) is used (single query) not N per-object queries

risks.impact: If POST /api/objects/labels/batch is registered after the per-object routes in objects.py, FastAPI may match 'labels' as an object_id literal in /api/objects/{object_id}/labels, routing the batch request to the wrong handler. Implementer must verify ordering.
200 objects × many labels fetched in one query result. At the 200-object cap this is expected to be manageable, but should be noted for future limit review if label density grows.
